'''Karin Melnick''' (born 1977) is an American mathematician and Professor at the [[University of Luxembourg]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Department of Mathematics {{!}} Melnick, Karin|url=https://www.uni.lu/fstm-en/people/karin-melnick/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=University of Luxembourg}}</ref> She specializes in differential geometry and was awarded the 2020–2021 Joan and Joseph Birman Fellowship for Women Scholars by the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref name=":0" />

==Research==
Melnick's primary research area is in differential-geometric aspects of rigidity, where she focuses on global and local results relating the automorphisms of a differential-geometric structure with the geometric and topological properties of the space.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Karin Melnick receives Birman Fellowship|url=https://www.ams.org/tools/news?news_id=6067|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=American Mathematical Society}}</ref> In addition, she is a leader in research in [[Lorentzian manifold|Lorentzian]] geometry and has done substantial work on the Lorentzian Lichnerowicz conjecture.<ref name=":0" />

Melnick also has research interests in conformal [[Pseudo-Riemannian manifold|pseudo-Riemannian]] structures, parabolic [[Cartan connection|Cartan]] geometries in general, and smooth dynamics.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Karin Melnick|url=https://math.uni.lu/~melnick/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=University of Luxembourg Department of Mathematics}}</ref>

==Education==
Melnick received her PhD in Mathematics from the [[University of Chicago]] in 2006, where she also earned her Master of Science in Mathematics in 2000, while working under the guidance of doctoral advisor [[Benson Farb]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Karin Melnick|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=104275|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> Her dissertation research focused on compact Lorentz manifolds with local symmetry.<ref name=":2" /> Prior to her graduate studies, Melnick received her Bachelor of Arts, also in Mathematics, from [[Reed College]] in 1999.<ref name=":1" />

==Career==
Melnick currently works as a professor in the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of Luxembourg]]. She was an assistant professor beginning in 2009 at the [[University of Maryland]], where she was promoted to associate professor in 2014 and to full professor in 2021. Before working at UMD, Melnick held the position of Gibbs Assistant Professor at [[Yale University]] while on an [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] Postdoctoral Research Fellowship.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=PostDoctoral Research Fellowship (Award Abstract #0603545)|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=0603545|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=National Science Foundation}}</ref>

==Honors==
Melnick was awarded the 2020–2021 Joan and Joseph Birman Fellowship for Women Scholars by the [[American Mathematical Society]] for her research on differential-geometric aspects of rigidity.<ref name=":0" /> This prestigious fellowship, founded by mathematician [[Joan Birman]] and physicist [[Joseph L. Birman]], is awarded to talented, mid-career women with a significant record of research in a core area of mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Joan and Joseph Birman Fellowship for Women Scholars|url=https://www.ams.org/prizes-awards/paview.cgi?parent_id=42|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=American Mathematical Society}}</ref>

Melnick has previously been awarded an [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|NSF CAREER Grant]] (2013), an [[AMS Centennial Fellowship]] (2012–2013), and a Junior Research Fellowship from the [[Erwin Schrödinger International Institute for Mathematical Physics|Erwin Schrödinger Institute]] (2009).<ref>{{Cite web|last=Jackson|first=Allyn|date=2012|title=2012–2013 AMS Centennial Fellowship Awarded|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201206/rtx120600844p.pdf|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=Notices of the AMS}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=CAREER: Frontiers of rigidity in pseudo-Riemannian, conformal, and parabolic geometries|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1255462|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=National Science Foundation Award Search}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2013|title=ESI Booklet|url=https://www.esi.ac.at/static/assets/extras/ESI_Booklet_2013.pdf|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=Erwin Schrödinger International Institute for Mathematical Physics}}</ref>
